lead: Chesapeake plumbing deals with a high water table, coastal storms and homes from the 1970s to 1990s boom. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Chesapeake.
risk: polybutylene pipe, flooding and backups, and well and septic systems in rural areas
risk_short: old pipes, flooding and septic systems
why: Chesapeake grew fast from the 1970s through the 1990s in Greenbrier, Great Bridge and Western Branch. Homes from the late 1970s to the mid-1990s may have gray polybutylene pipe.
Low ground and a high water table mean nor'easters and hurricanes flood streets and back up drains. Rural southern Chesapeake has many homes on wells and septic systems.
water: Chesapeake treats water from the Northwest River and buys water from neighboring cities. It is moderately soft. Rural homes outside the system use private wells.
tips: Look for gray pipe stamped PB2110.
Check crawl-space drainage after big storms.
Have your well water tested yearly if you have a well.
areas: PipeMend works in Greenbrier, Great Bridge, Western Branch, Deep Creek, South Norfolk, Hickory, Grassfield and every other Chesapeake neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Chesapeake Department of Development and Permits, and plumbers must hold a tradesman license from the Virginia Board for Contractors (DPOR).

faq.q: Do many Chesapeake homes have polybutylene pipe?
faq.a: Many homes built from the late 1970s to the mid-1990s do, when the city grew fast. Look for gray plastic pipe stamped PB2110. Replacing it before it fails avoids water damage.
